page_title: Tapflow / 点流 —— 你的个性化控制层

summary.name: Tapflow
summary.one_liner: Tapflow (点流) turns an iPad into a customizable touch input panel for controlling a Mac, served from a Mac server and opened in a browser.
use_cases: Replace hard-to-remember keyboard shortcuts with on-screen buttons
Start and stop voice input while coding with AI tools
Snap and maximize Mac windows with gestures
Switch between windows using live thumbnails
Control a Mac from an iPad over local WiFi
summary.what_it_does: Tapflow runs a server on a Mac and lets a tablet, phone or any browser on the same local network connect to it at http://<Mac-IP>:8082 with no app install needed. Users drag, resize and style buttons in a WYSIWYG editor, grouping and naming them with colors, icons and sounds, and can switch layouts automatically per app via profiles. Built-in components cover window snapping by swipe gestures, a live-thumbnail window switcher, a Dock panel, audio output selection and a microphone level indicator. Each touch is sent over WebSocket and injected into macOS using CGEvent, and some buttons can also display output such as a DeepSeek balance.
notable: Tablet or phone connects via browser with no app install, over the same LAN only
Live-thumbnail window switcher grouped by app, plus swipe-based window snapping
Profiles switch the panel layout automatically when the active app changes
Open source code; buttons can show outgoing info such as AI service balances
caveats: Requires macOS 26+ on Apple Silicon (M1 or newer); Mac-only backend
v1 is an early-bird validation stage, described as free; not notarized, so Gatekeeper requires a one-time manual approval
Needs Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions; microphone is optional
Other AI tool integrations are said to be added gradually
